files.role: Pure event reducer / state machine: validates and folds one journal event at a time into cycle state; owns all cross-event invariants and the closed-ledger derivation.

Schema/shape validators and canonical digest helpers for fixture actions, owner approvals, post-open buyback approvals, and provider receipts; embeds the fixed fixture action policy and the fixed test Ed25519 provider public key.
Canonical JSON + SHA-256 digesting, bounded-recursion guards (RECOVERY_LIMITS), and the CycleJournal class implementing the hash-chained append-only journal.

In-memory durable store: FixtureCycleStore (per-cycle journal snapshot, authorization records, receipt records) plus FixtureCycleTransaction implementing compare-and-swap commit of one batch of journal events + authorization/receipt consumption.

Facade class CycleRunner: recovers state from (journal entries, store) on construction, then exposes ~25 one-call-per-event-kind command methods that build a journal event, replay it through the reducer against a transaction, and commit atomically.

purpose: Together these five files implement a durable, event-sourced, compare-and-swap state machine for exactly one Phase-1 HKMN pack cycle: outbound (vault USDG -> policy-account Circle USD), purchase (Collector Crypt pack, quantity 1, non-turbo), open (pack draw / NFT reveal), buyback (standard Collector buyback of the drawn card back to Circle USD), return (Circle USD -> vault USDG), then distribution-verification and vault-payout-funding preparation. Every external interaction (Collector Crypt API, Solana RPC, transaction signing/broadcast) is modeled as a 'fixture' envelope verified against one hardcoded test Ed25519 key -- there is no live provider/RPC/bridge integration in these files, and CycleRunner.verifyProductionProviderReceipt() unconditionally throws 'INTEGRATION_PENDING'. The module has no timer, scheduler, HTTP surface, or dashboard: every state advance is one explicit, individually authorized method call.

(collector-status-consumed is explicitly rejected as a 'legacy' unauthenticated kind; any unlisted kind hits default and throws 'unknown journal event'.)

deriveReturnedProceedsKey(state, receiptDigest), readClosedProceedsBasisHandoff(state, proceedsKey), deriveVaultPayoutAuthorization(state, receipt, {expiresAt,nonce}), externalMutationIdentity(state, requestDigest), externalReconciliationEvidence(state, requestDigest), signedBytesDigest({messageDigest, signedBytes})

assertVerifiedOwnerApproval(value), assertVerifiedPostOpenBuybackApproval(value) -- NOTE: reducer.mjs actually imports the *authorization-verifying* equivalents (verifyFixtureAuthorization / verifyFixturePostOpenBuybackAuthorization) from ./authorization.mjs, not these two; these two look like the underlying shape-only validators that authorization.mjs presumably wraps with signature checks.

fixtureReceiptVerificationDigest(value), assertVerifiedProviderReceipt(value) (checks Ed25519 signature against a hardcoded providerPublicKey), receiptIdentityKey(receipt), receiptRegistryRecord(receipt, receiptDigest), assertReceiptRelationship(receipt, action, execution)
journal.mjs: class CycleJournal(cycleId, entries=[]) { get head/cycleId/entries; propose(kind,payload)->entry; appendEvent(entry); append(kind,payload); prepareIntent({actionKind,request,bindingDigest}) [see suspicion: unused/dead, appends kind 'intent' which the reducer does not recognize]; verify() }
cycle-store.mjs: class FixtureCycleStore(snapshot) { static reopen(snapshot); get snapshot; readCycle(cycleId); authorizationRecord(key); authorizationKeyForNonce(nonceKey); receiptRecord(key); begin(cycleId,{expectedVersion,expectedJournalHead}) -> FixtureCycleTransaction; commit(transaction) }

class FixtureCycleTransaction (internal, constructed only via store.begin) { stageEvent(value); consumeAuthorization(value)->key; consumeReceipt(value)->key; consume(value) [alias of consumeReceipt]; authorizationRecord(key); receiptRecord(key); assertStagedRecordsPersisted(); get stagedEvents/stagedAuthorizations/stagedReceipts; close() }
cycle-runner.mjs: class CycleRunner(cycleId, entries=[], {cycleStore}) -- constructor replays entries through the reducer against a store transaction; if the store's persisted version is 0 it stages+commits all given entries as new; otherwise it requires the given entries to canonically equal the store's persisted entries and only asserts staged (already-persisted) records still match.
static recover(cycleId, entries, options) = new CycleRunner(...)
get entries / get cycleStoreSnapshot / get state ({stage,version,journalHead})

Command methods (each = one journal event via private #commit): recordReleasedCyclePreflight, prepareExternalIntent, recordOwnerAuthorization, consumeAuthorizationOnce, recordFixtureDecodedTransaction, recordSignedBytes, recordFixtureBlockhashValidity, broadcastPreparedTransactionOnce, appendCanonicalReceipt, recordExecutionAccountingEvidence, consumeReceiptOnce, advanceCycleState, deriveOpenReconciliation, deriveClosedCycle, close (=deriveClosedCycle), consumeReturnedProceedsOnce, readClosedProceedsBasisHandoff, recordDistributionVerification, preparePayoutFunding, reconcileUnresolvedIntent, executeAuthorizedExternalMutationOnce, prepareCollectorGenerateIntent, prepareCollectorOpenIntent, consumeCollectorMutationAuthorization, recordVerifiedCollectorStatus, recordFinalizedCollectorOpenCustody, generateCollectorPack, recordCollectorStatus (always throws -- legacy path removed), openCollectorPack, recordPostOpenBuybackAuthorization, verifyProductionProviderReceipt (always throws INTEGRATION_PENDING).
publicInterface.cliCommands: None. No CLI, HTTP endpoint, or scheduler is defined in any of the five files; all functionality is a JS library API meant to be driven by an external caller/test.
publicInterface.events: See reduceCycleEvent switch list above -- that list is the exhaustive vocabulary of durable journal event kinds.
publicInterface.errors: All failures are plain `throw new Error('...')` with descriptive fail-closed messages; there are no custom Error subclasses or error codes.

invariants: Two-layer compare-and-swap: (1) FixtureCycleStore.commit rejects a transaction whose expectedVersion/expectedJournalHead do not match the store's current persisted cycle row; (2) reducer.transition() separately requires payload.expectedVersion===state.version and payload.expectedJournalHead===state.head===event.previousDigest before allowing a stage transition.

Journal integrity: every entry's digest is recomputed and compared (assertJournalEntry) on propose, append, and full replay; canonicalJson rejects prototypes, symbols, cycles, -0, bigint, sparse/decorated arrays and __proto__/prototype/constructor keys, so a hash-valid but structurally-tampered entry cannot pass.

Exactly-once external mutation attempts: externalMutationAttempted forbids starting a second unresolved mutation while one is outstanding and forbids ever re-attempting the same requestDigest once it exists in state.externalMutations (no blind retry) -- only externalMutationReconciled (fed by independently verified provider+RPC evidence) can close out an attempt.

Fixed, non-negotiable per-action shape and amounts: assertFixtureActionPolicy hardcodes source/destination/asset/mint/tokenAccount and amount='10'/minimumReceive='10'/nativeGasAmount='1'/principalAmount='10' for every outbound/purchase/buyback/return action; only binding-derived accounts (execution wallet, refund token account) vary.

Wallet-binding immutability: the first fixture action fixes executionWallet/refundTokenAccount/refundTokenAccountOwner for the whole cycle; a later action with a different binding is rejected (verifyIntent).

5 distinct single-use authorization kinds per action (mutation/sign/broadcast/asset-spend/gas-spend), each bound to a different subject digest (actionDigest, decoded messageDigest, or signedBytesDigest respectively) and each consumed exactly once via FixtureCycleTransaction.consumeAuthorization, which also enforces global nonce uniqueness across the whole store.

Receipts are globally unique by (provider, providerReceiptId) via receiptIdentityKey, checked both in-cycle (state.receiptIdentities) and across the whole store/across recovery (FixtureCycleStore keeps receipt records keyed by that identity and refuses divergent content for the same key).

Finalized block-height monotonicity: verifyReceipt enforces state.finalizedBlockHeight is non-decreasing across the whole cycle; validateClosedLedger additionally enforces the strict per-step order purchase < collector-open-custody < buyback in block height.

Native gas accounting: per-chain reserved (at intent time) and actual (at accounting time) gas are both tracked against preflight.nativeGasCaps[chain]; validateClosedLedger recomputes actual usage from the four execution-accounting records and requires it to equal the running nativeGasUsed and stay under cap.

Closed-ledger derivation (validateClosedLedger) re-derives full custody continuity independently of any label: exact vault USDG debit = principal; adjacent-action handoff continuity (assertLedgerHandoff) for outbound->purchase, purchase->buyback (cross-asset, Circle USD->NFT), buyback->return; NFT mint/custody continuity from purchase deposit through open debit/credit to buyback debit/credit into the Collector prize wallet; and a final activity-isolated USDG credit whose account-activity window is bound by exact block hash from the buyback block through the return block.

Distribution/payout gating: recordDistributionVerification requires a matching closed ledger + consumed proceeds key; preparePayoutFunding/prepareFunding independently re-derives the vault payout authorization (deriveVaultPayoutAuthorization) and requires byte-identical match plus its own single-use 'vault-payout' authorization consumption and an expiry check; the returned object is explicitly tagged authority: 'LOCAL_PREPARATION_ONLY_NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY', and readClosedProceedsBasisHandoff is tagged 'READ_ONLY_SELF_CONSISTENT_NOT_STORE_MEMBERSHIP_PROOF' -- i.e. the code itself documents that these outputs are not proof of durable membership/authority and must not be trusted as such by a caller.

Recovery never trusts direct journal appends: CycleRunner's constructor always replays every given entry through reduceCycleEvent against a real store transaction; if the store already has a persisted version, the given entries must canonically equal the persisted ones or construction throws.
stateTransitions: transitionOrder = [prepared, outbound-finalized, purchase-finalized, open-reconciled, buyback-finalized, return-finalized, closed] -- strictly linear, one-directional, no branch/rollback state.
outbound-finalized needs consumed+reconciled outbound receipt; purchase-finalized additionally needs consumed+reconciled purchase receipt.

open-reconciled needs both Collector generate and open intents+authorizations+response+verified status+opened+openExecution+openCustody complete AND both their external mutations externally-reconciled, on top of the outbound+purchase prefix (no new receipt kind here -- it's the Collector custody proof, not a fixture action).
buyback-finalized adds the consumed+reconciled buyback receipt (which itself required a separate post-open-buyback-approval-consumed event beyond the generic mutation authorization).
return-finalized adds the consumed+reconciled return receipt.

closed re-validates the entire ledger from scratch (validateClosedLedger) and additionally requires state.externalMutations.size===6 (4 actions + collector-generate + collector-open), all six reconciled, and every collection's size to exactly equal the expected cardinality (no leftover/unmatched proceeds, actions, approvals, receipts).

Post-closure, non-transitionOrder progressions exist as separate independent event kinds gated by state.stage==='closed': proceeds-consumed (once, keyed to the exact final-credit receipt+ledger digest) -> distribution-verification-recorded (once, must reference that exact proceeds key + closed ledger digest) -> payout-funding-prepared (once, must reference that exact distribution-verification receipt).

Crash/restart: CycleRunner(cycleId, journalEntries, {cycleStore}) reconstructs state purely by replaying the journal through reduceCycleEvent; an externally-attempted-but-unresolved mutation survives recovery as 'unresolved' and can only be advanced by reconcileUnresolvedIntent supplying fresh provider+RPC evidence -- the runner never assumes a mid-flight external action succeeded or failed on its own.

externalDependencies.pinnedLibraries: node:crypto only (createHash, createPublicKey, verify) -- both schemas.mjs and journal.mjs are pure Node built-ins with zero npm dependencies. No @solana/web3.js, no HTTP client, no fetch, no bridge/relay SDK anywhere in these five files.
externalDependencies.providers: None wired live. All 'provider' interaction is the string literal 'fixture-provider' checked against a single hardcoded test Ed25519 public key embedded in schemas.mjs (providerPublicKey). Collector Crypt, Solana RPC, and the USDG<->Circle USD conversion/bridge are all represented as fixture envelopes with no network call anywhere in these files.

testStatus.characterization: All executed suites pass cleanly with zero skipped/todo tests. Nothing here is compile-only or disabled. Every test drives the same fixture Ed25519 keys and fixture accounts baked into schemas.mjs -- there is no test that exercises a real Collector Crypt API call, a real Solana RPC, or a real Robinhood-chain transaction; test coverage validates the state-machine/security invariants of the fixture harness itself, not production integration correctness (which is explicitly out of scope per verifyProductionProviderReceipt()'s INTEGRATION_PENDING throw).

autonomyGaps: No scheduler/timer/cron/loop anywhere in these five files. Nothing triggers 'buy a pack every N minutes'; every CycleRunner method is a single manual call. The owner's 'every 20 minutes, adjustable in a dashboard' requirement has zero implementation here -- it would need an external orchestrator (not present in this worktree) driving CycleRunner in a loop.

No dashboard, HTTP/API surface, or UI of any kind. 'choose which packs to buy', 'change the interval', 'restart/kick stuck cycles', 'community-facing status' have no corresponding methods or endpoints in this module.

No live provider/RPC/chain integration. Collector Crypt generate/open, Solana RPC finality, and provider receipt verification are all fixture envelopes checked against one hardcoded test Ed25519 key; CycleRunner.verifyProductionProviderReceipt() unconditionally throws 'INTEGRATION_PENDING'. None of outbound/purchase/open/buyback/return can execute against a real chain today.

Every state advance requires a distinct, pre-signed, single-use 'fixture owner approval' -- 5 authorization kinds x 4 actions (20) + 2 Collector mutation authorizations (generate/open) + 1 post-open buyback authorization + 1 vault-payout authorization = 24 individually signed owner approvals per single cycle. This is structurally a human-in-the-loop / ask-first design, the opposite of 'fully autonomous' -- true unattended operation needs an automated signer/policy-wallet service that is not present in these files (the repository facts describe such a service existing only in the unmerged codex/complete-v4-hook branch, outside this worktree).

No parameterization of pack choice, quantity, or interval: FIXTURE_ACTION_POLICY hardcodes exactly one pack shape and fixed amount ('10' units) per action kind; nothing here reads a 'chosen pack' or 'chosen interval' input.

No 'stuck cycle' detection/alerting/manual-override API beyond generic journal replay and reconcileUnresolvedIntent (which only advances when real external evidence appears -- there is no forced-abort or forced-resolve path). This matches the docs' explicit statement that 'a stranded vault cycle...remains explicit thin-V1 state; recovery requires manual reconciliation or a later approved specification,' i.e. autonomous self-healing is explicitly deferred, not a bug.

No pro-rata holder distribution execution: preparePayoutFunding only produces a local, non-authoritative payout-funding record (authority: 'LOCAL_PREPARATION_ONLY_NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY'). The actual on-chain payout, and the merkle/holder-snapshot math implementing 'distributed pro rata to HKMN holders automatically', live in ../distribution/manifest.mjs and reconcile.mjs, outside this unit, and even there this module only prepares, never executes, funding.

The 3%/0.5%/2.5% fee-split economics the owner described are entirely absent from these files -- principalAmount/spend-cap here come from an opaque preflight record (verifyFixtureCyclePreflight, not read) rather than any visible process-budget percentage computation.

suspicions.note: CycleJournal.prepareIntent({actionKind,request,bindingDigest}) is defined but has zero call sites anywhere in the repo (grep across packages/runner confirms only its own definition). It appends a journal event of kind 'intent', but reduceCycleEvent's switch in reducer.mjs (lines 1144-1172) has no 'intent' case -- only 'intent-prepared' -- so calling this method and feeding its event into the reducer would fall through to the default branch and throw 'unknown journal event intent'. All real intent creation instead goes through CycleRunner.prepareExternalIntent, which calls journal.propose('intent-prepared', ...) directly, bypassing prepareIntent entirely. This looks like dead/orphaned code from an earlier event-naming scheme that should be deleted or reconciled so the journal module's advertised API doesn't silently produce reducer-incompatible events.

In verifyApproval, the guard requiring a separate post-open buyback authorization ('separate post-open buyback authorization is required') is only checked when state.collector.generated is truthy: `if (state.collector.generated && prepared.action.actionKind === 'buyback' && approval.authorizationKind === 'mutation' && !state.postOpenBuybackApproval) throw ...`. Given actionStage.get('buyback')==='open-reconciled' and open-reconciled requires collector.generated to be set (checked in evidenceForTransition), this is very likely unreachable as a real hole today, but the guard's own correctness silently depends on that separate, non-local invariant rather than checking state.stage directly here. Worth an explicit reviewer confirmation that no future refactor of the stage-ordering could let a buyback mutation approval through before collector.generated is set.

providerPublicKey is a single hardcoded Ed25519 SPKI DER blob compiled into the module (no rotation, no config, no comment identifying it as a test-only fixture key beyond the surrounding 'fixture-provider' naming convention). Confirm nothing outside the test suite ever imports or treats this constant as anything other than a disposable fixture key before any production wiring lands.

cycle-store.mjs re-implements its own 'exact schema' plain-object validator (exactObject) that duplicates the logic of schemas.mjs's assertPlainObject (schemas.mjs:39-45) almost line for line, in a separate file with no shared helper. Today the behavior appears equivalent, but the duplication is a maintenance risk if one copy's exactness/limit checks are updated without the other.

keyFacts: transitionOrder: prepared -> outbound-finalized -> purchase-finalized -> open-reconciled -> buyback-finalized -> return-finalized -> closed (reducer.mjs:44).

cycleActionKinds = [outbound, purchase, buyback, return] (4); actionAuthorizationKinds = [mutation, sign, broadcast, asset-spend, gas-spend] (5) => 20 per-action owner approvals + 2 Collector mutation authorizations (generate, open) + 1 post-open-buyback authorization + 1 vault-payout authorization = 24 single-use signed authorizations required for one full closed cycle (reducer.mjs:51-52, validateClosedLedger).
state.externalMutations.size must equal exactly 6 at closure: the 4 fixture actions plus collector-generate plus collector-open (reducer.mjs:476).
Fixed Circle Circle USD mint used as the Solana-side settlement asset: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, 6 decimals, Solana mainnet-beta (schemas.mjs:12, docs/modules/cycle-runner.md).

Placeholder EVM-style fixture addresses (clearly synthetic, not real Robinhood Chain addresses): FIXTURE_OPERATIONS_TRIGGER=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001004, FIXTURE_CYCLE_VAULT_ACCOUNT=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001002 (schemas.mjs:9-10).

Every fixture action is hardcoded to principalAmount='10', minimumReceive='10', nativeGasAmount='1', amount='10' -- fixed-size unit transfers, not driven by any live pack price or process-budget percentage (schemas.mjs:113-127, assertFixtureActionPolicy).

External confirmation (grep, preflight.mjs, not fully read): the funded-cycle preflight requires requirementsRevision===56, chainId==='4663' (Robinhood Chain, matches repository facts), asset==='USDG', finalized===true.

RECOVERY_LIMITS bounds (journal.mjs:4-29): max 512 journal events/cycle, 16 cycles/store, 128 authorizations/store, 64 receipts/store; canonicalDepth 32; canonicalAggregateBytes 2 MiB; per-journal-payload aggregateBytes 256 KiB; instructions<=16/action, accountsPerInstruction<=64, signers<=16; decimalDigits<=78; hexChars<=131072 (message)/262144 (signed bytes).

Provider receipt signature check: node:crypto verify(null, Buffer.from(fixtureVerificationDigest,'utf8'), providerPublicKey, Buffer.from(signature,'base64url')) -- i.e. raw/PureEdDSA verification over the UTF-8 bytes of the 'sha256:<hex>' digest STRING, not over the raw 32 binary hash bytes (schemas.mjs:284). Anyone reimplementing a real signer must reproduce this exact string-encoding convention.

FIXTURE_AUTHORIZATION_VALIDATED_AT (imported constant from ./authorization.mjs) is used as the single frozen 'current time' for every expiry/consumption check in the module -- the whole fixture harness runs against one fixed clock instant rather than Date.now().
